question.problem:
If ${X}_{1}∼N(7,5)$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(8,4)$ are independent and $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2},$ calculate $P(-1.9\le Y<-0.49).$ Round your final answer to two decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.3\,$ $\,0.3821\,$ $\,0.3783\,$ $\,0.3745\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$z$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$
$\,0.1\,$ $\,0.5596\,$ $\,0.5636\,$ $\,0.5675\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.5987\,$ $\,0.6026\,$ $\,0.6064\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6368\,$ $\,0.6406\,$ $\,0.6443\,$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2} & ∼N({\mu }_{1}-{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(7-8,5+4) \\  & ∼N(-1,9).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =-1$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{9}=3.$ 

We want to find $P(-1.9\le Y<-0.49).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.9\le Y<0.49) & =P(\frac{-1.9-(-1)}{3}\le Z<\frac{-0.49-(-1)}{3}) \\  & =P(-0.3\le Z<0.17) \\  & =P(Z<0.17)-P(Z<-0.3) \\  & =Φ(0.17)-Φ(-0.3)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.3) & ≈0.3821 \\ Φ(0.17) & ≈0.5675\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.9\le Y<0.49) & =Φ(0.17)-Φ(-0.3) \\  & ≈0.5675-0.3821 \\  & ≈0.19.\end{aligned}
$$
